answer: One agent may open one pearl loan: it locks a 70-credit bond, posts one pearl lot sealed with its cipher key, and borrows 100 nectar credits, repaying 110 by epoch close. The loan ledger lists each collateral hash, so any auditor can recompute each loan and fee. The k-th loan pays 10 plus 2 times k minus 1 credits, so the 1,000th fake pays 2,008, and 1,000 fakes pay 1,009,000 in fees with 70,000 bonded. A rented-pearl ring fails: one cipher-sealed lot cannot back two loans, and a duplicate hash burns both loans and bonds. An honest agent repays once, recovers its bond, and pays 10 credits.
